adventure.title: Ferry to Angel Island, Climb Mount Livermore
adventure.description: The ferry drops you on the bay's biggest island — hike to the 788-foot summit for a 360 of the entire bay, then walk the immigration station where the Pacific's Ellis Island story is carved into the walls.
adventure.bonus: Summit before lunch and name every bridge you can see — there are five on a clear day.

adventure.title: Take the Secret Stairways of the Haight to Twin Peaks
adventure.description: SF has over 400 public stairways and the chain from the Upper Haight through Ashbury Heights to Twin Peaks summit is the city's most rewarding hidden spine.
adventure.bonus: Reach the top of Red Rock and face into the wind with both arms out for a full 30 seconds.

adventure.title: Climb the Filbert Steps to Coit Tower at Sunrise
adventure.description: The wooden boardwalk staircase through wild parrots and hidden cottage gardens is the most cinematic 5 a.m. commute in any American city.
adventure.bonus: Spot a wild cherry-headed conure in the trees — photograph it within arm's reach if you can.

adventure.title: Cross the Golden Gate on Foot in Golden Light
adventure.description: Walking the bridge in the last full hour of afternoon sun — Marin Headlands glowing, city stacking up behind you — rewires your sense of scale. Check the sidewalk hours and beat the gate.
adventure.bonus: Stop exactly at the midpoint, face the open ocean, and say out loud the one thing you want most right now.

adventure.title: Ride the 16th Avenue Tiled Steps to Grand View Park
adventure.description: The mosaic staircase is just the warm-up — keep climbing through the hidden garden to Grand View Park's summit for the best unobstructed city panorama in the Sunset.
adventure.bonus: Count every tiled step on the way down without losing track — there are 163.

adventure.title: Kayak Under the Bay Bridge at McCovey Cove
adventure.description: City Kayak launches you into the inner bay where the bridge towers overhead and the skyline sits close enough to feel impossible.
adventure.bonus: Paddle directly under a bridge tower, look straight up, and stay there for 60 seconds without drifting.

adventure.title: Walk the Sutro Baths Ruins at Low Tide
adventure.description: The collapsed Victorian bathhouse pools fill and drain with the ocean tide, and at low tide the ruins become a maze you can actually walk through.
adventure.bonus: Find the sea cave tunnel at the north end and walk all the way through it to the ocean side.

adventure.title: Scramble Up Corona Heights for a 360 View
adventure.description: This rocky Buena Vista-adjacent peak is a five-minute scramble that earns you an unobstructed panorama most tourists never find.
adventure.bonus: Climb the highest exposed rock at the summit and stay up there until someone else arrives.

adventure.title: Explore Alcatraz After Dark on the Night Tour
adventure.description: The island prison transforms at night — rangers guide you through cellblocks with only your footsteps and the bay wind for company.
adventure.bonus: Stand alone in the solitary confinement cell — D-Block, cell 14 — for one full minute in the dark.

adventure.title: Bike the Golden Gate Bridge to Sausalito
adventure.description: Rent a bike at Fisherman's Wharf, cross the bridge in the wind, and coast down into Sausalito for a ferry ride back across the bay.
adventure.bonus: Stop mid-bridge, grip the railing, and look straight down at the water for a full 30 seconds.

adventure.title: Dawn Patrol at Ocean Beach
adventure.description: SF's wild, ungroomed beach hits different at sunrise when the fog is still low and the surfers are already reading the break.
adventure.bonus: Wade in past your knees — the water is colder than you expect and that's the point.

adventure.title: Hike Land's End Trail to the Labyrinth
adventure.description: The rugged coastal trail along the Marin Headlands lip delivers broken sea views, shipwreck ghosts, and a hidden stone labyrinth perched above the Pacific.
adventure.bonus: Walk the labyrinth to the center in complete silence, then turn around and do it backwards.

foodie.title: The Cart at House of Prime Rib
foodie.description: Since 1949 the silver zeppelin carts have rolled tableside on Van Ness carving prime rib to order — martinis built at the table, spinning salad bowls, and zero interest in the year outside.
foodie.bonus: Say yes when they offer seconds — that's the whole point of the cart.

foodie.title: Focaccia Squares at Golden Boy Pizza
foodie.description: Since 1978 this North Beach slot in the wall has sold thick Ligurian focaccia squares — clam and garlic, pesto — through a window framed in punk stickers. Cash, line, no seats worth wanting.
foodie.bonus: Clam and garlic square, eaten leaning on the parklet, no napkin dignity required.

foodie.title: Explore the Ferry Building Marketplace on a Saturday
foodie.description: The Saturday farmers market wrapping around the 1898 Ferry Building brings the best of Northern California's farms, cheeses, and oyster bars to one waterfront hall.
foodie.bonus: Build your entire breakfast from vendors outside — no sitting down, just graze and walk.

foodie.title: Pizza and Natural Wine at Flour + Water
foodie.description: This Mission stalwart has been making some of the most technically precise pasta and Neapolitan-style pizza in the city since 2009 — walk-ins at the bar still work.
foodie.bonus: Eat at the bar alone and strike up a real conversation with whoever sits next to you.

foodie.title: Ramen at Marufuku, Japantown
foodie.description: The Japan Center institution whose Hakata-style tonkotsu draws the longest, most patient lines in the city — thin noodles, milky broth, no shortcuts.
foodie.bonus: Add every available topping without checking the price — live dangerously, it's ramen.

foodie.title: Mission Burrito Crawl on 24th Street
foodie.description: La Taqueria versus El Farolito is San Francisco's oldest civic debate — walk the two blocks between them and settle it for yourself.
foodie.bonus: Order the exact same burrito at both — same protein, same toppings — and declare a winner out loud to a stranger.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Saison
foodie.description: A wood-fire-driven tasting menu in SoMa where every course feels like the chef is quietly showing off — and absolutely winning.
foodie.bonus: Tell your server one ingredient you genuinely dislike and see how they handle it — the kitchen's response will tell you everything.

foodie.title: Crab Louie at Swan Oyster Depot
foodie.description: This 1912 seafood counter on Polk Street runs on pure institution energy — eighteen marble stools, crushed ice, cold Anchor Steam, and the freshest Dungeness crab in the city.
foodie.bonus: Ask the guy behind the counter what he'd eat today — then order exactly that.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Tartine Bakery
foodie.description: The line snaking down Guerrero Street is your first sign that the morning buns and country bread here are worth every minute of the wait.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever the baker is pulling fresh from the oven right now — no menu browsing, just point and commit.

foodie.title: Sourdough Tasting at Boudin Bakery Fisherman's Wharf
foodie.description: The 170-year-old mother dough behind this bakery is arguably the most important starter in American bread history and you can taste it in a proper loaf pulled fresh from the oven.
foodie.bonus: Buy a loaf, tear it open right outside, and eat the entire warm center before you leave the block.

foodie.title: Dim Sum at Yank Sing in the Financial District
foodie.description: Rolling carts, 100-plus items, and har gow so good it settles arguments — this Rincon Center institution has been the city's dim sum benchmark since 1958.
foodie.bonus: Order one item you cannot identify and eat it completely before asking what it was.

foodie.title: Lunch at Zuni Café
foodie.description: The brick-oven roast chicken for two with warm bread salad has been San Francisco's defining meal since 1979 and no one has topped it.
foodie.bonus: Order the chicken for one — they'll resist, but hold firm — and eat every last piece at the zinc bar.

active.title: Sunday Skate at the Skatin' Place
active.description: Every Sunday since the seventies, Golden Gate Park's dedicated roller rink pavement off JFK fills with disco skaters, boom boxes, and anyone brave enough to join the circle.
active.bonus: Enter the circle for at least one full song.

active.title: Lap the Track at Kezar Stadium
active.description: The public track inside the old 49ers stadium on the edge of Golden Gate Park has hosted everyone from Olympians to lunchtime shufflers — free, historic, and open to whoever shows up.
active.bonus: One mile timed — then one victory lap in the outside lane like the old stadium is full.

active.title: Repeats on the Lyon Street Steps
active.description: The manicured staircase dropping from Pacific Heights to the Palace of Fine Arts is the city's glammest outdoor gym — sweat alongside the 6 a.m. regulars with the bay filling the view.
active.bonus: Five full climbs — no pausing at the hedge garden to pretend you're admiring it.

active.title: Gravel Ride the Marin Headlands Loop
active.description: A punishing 25-mile mixed-surface loop through the Headlands delivers military ruins, hawk thermals, and enough climbing to hollow you out completely before the descent back to the Golden Gate.
active.bonus: Ride without stopping at the summit — earn the view, then take a photo to prove you made it.

active.title: Paddle Board the Bay from Crissy Field
active.description: Launching from Crissy Field puts you on the water with direct views of the Golden Gate, Alcatraz, and the Marin Headlands in one of the world's most dramatic urban waterways.
active.bonus: Paddle far enough to put the bridge directly overhead and sit still for 60 seconds.

active.title: Sunrise at Baker Beach Under the Golden Gate
active.description: Watching the Golden Gate materialize through the fog from Baker Beach at first light is a private, cinematic moment that most tourists sleeping in never see.
active.bonus: Walk to the north end of the beach and wade into the surf up to your knees — fog or shine.

active.title: Hike Mount Tamalpais East Peak via Steep Ravine
active.description: The Steep Ravine Trail through old-growth redwoods and up to Tam's 2,571-foot summit delivers one of the most dramatic half-day hikes within an hour of the city.
active.bonus: Summit before 9am — name every body of water you can see from the top.

active.title: Morning Tai Chi at Portsmouth Square
active.description: Chinatown's living room fills with dozens of locals running tai chi and fan routines at dawn, a completely unselfconscious ritual that's been happening here for generations.
active.bonus: Step into the edge of a group and mirror the movements for at least 10 minutes without stopping.

active.title: Bouldering at Dogpatch Boulders
active.description: San Francisco's only dedicated bouldering gym drops you into a tight, technical climbing community where regulars push hard problems and strangers spot each other without being asked.
active.bonus: Ask a stranger to beta a V4 or harder and attempt it before you leave.

active.title: Swim at Aquatic Park Cove with the Dolphin Club
active.description: The sheltered saltwater cove at the foot of Ghirardelli Square is where year-round swimmers brave the 55-degree bay without wetsuits — buy a day pass at the Dolphin Club or South End Rowing Club and earn your membership in the conversation.
active.bonus: Get in without testing the water first — no toe-dipping, just go.

active.title: Morning Run on the Embarcadero to Oracle Park
active.description: The flat waterfront stretch from the Ferry Building south to Oracle Park delivers bay views, sea air, and the satisfying emptiness of a city not yet awake.
active.bonus: Run the whole stretch without earbuds — just the bay, the gulls, and your own breathing.

active.title: Run the Panhandle to Ocean Beach and Back
active.description: The Panhandle to Great Highway route runs six miles through Golden Gate Park's core — redwood groves, buffalo paddock, and a beach finish — and it's the local runner's standard.
active.bonus: Sprint the last 200 meters to the ocean, touch the water, and don't stop until your feet are wet.

social.title: Stand-Up at the Punch Line
social.description: SF's longest-running comedy club has been a proving ground since 1978 — Robin Williams worked this room, Ali Wong taped here, and Tuesday showcases still launch careers.
social.bonus: Sit close enough to be crowd-worked and take it with grace.

social.title: Roller Disco at the Church of 8 Wheels
social.description: A deconsecrated Fillmore church reborn as a roller disco — stained glass, funk on the speakers, and Godfather of Skate David Miles Jr. presiding over the congregation.
social.bonus: Stay on wheels the entire session — pew breaks are for quitters.

social.title: Negroni at Nopa on Divisadero
social.description: Open until 1am every night since 2006, Nopa's counter seats are the best perch in SF for a perfectly built Negroni and an unscripted conversation with whoever's next to you.
social.bonus: Sit at the counter alone and order the thing you'd never normally order.

social.title: Attend a Giants Game at Oracle Park
social.description: Oracle Park sits on the bay with a view that makes bad baseball feel like a privilege — get a Ghirardelli sundae in the fourth inning and commit fully to the ritual.
social.bonus: Sit in the bleachers and start a conversation with the person directly to your left before the first pitch.

social.title: Drop Into Shotwell's Bar in the Mission
social.description: A no-frills neighborhood bar since 1891 with cheap drinks, a pool table, and a jukebox that knows the neighborhood — exactly the kind of place SF keeps trying to replace.
social.bonus: Challenge a regular to a game of pool for the next round.

social.title: Attend a Reading at Green Apple Books
social.description: Inner Richmond's beloved two-store independent hosts author readings that attract serious literary crowds in a setting that smells exactly like a bookstore should.
social.bonus: Buy the author's book and get it signed — ask them one question that isn't about the book.

social.title: Cocktail Class at Trick Dog in the Mission
social.description: One of the most consistently creative cocktail bars in America rotates its menu around absurd conceptual themes and employs bartenders who can outdrink most sommeliers on knowledge alone.
social.bonus: Order blind — tell the bartender your mood in one word and accept whatever arrives.

social.title: Drink the List at Vesuvio Café
social.description: Jack Kerouac's preferred North Beach bar has barely changed since 1948 — two floors of mismatched tables, Beat-era art, and a jukebox that earns its spot on the wall.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with the person next to you and find out what they're writing, building, or running from.

social.title: Late Night Karaoke at The Mint
social.description: The Castro's beloved karaoke bar has been running nonstop since 1989 and the crowd on a Friday night turns every song into a full room event.
social.bonus: Sign up for a song before you've had your first drink — commit to it stone cold sober.

social.title: Afternoon Pint at Toronado on Haight Street
social.description: This no-nonsense craft beer bar has been pouring exceptional drafts since 1987 — the tap list is absurdly good and the vibe is pure unironic dive.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender for whatever they're personally most excited about right now — no arguing with the answer.

social.title: Catch a Show at The Fillmore
social.description: Opened in 1912 and the launchpad for Jimi Hendrix, Janis Joplin, and the Grateful Dead — the Fillmore's room acoustics and psychedelic poster walls still make every show feel historic.
social.bonus: Grab a free apple from the barrel at the door, make it to the front of the crowd, and don't leave until the house lights come up.

social.title: Bar Crawl Through the Tenderloin's Dive Bar Row
social.description: Larkin Street between Geary and O'Farrell is a string of unreconstructed dive bars where the drinks are cheap, the regulars are lifers, and the stories are real.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the strangers at the bar at your second stop — no explanation required.

chill.title: Feed Quarters to the Musée Mécanique
chill.description: A working arcade of 300 antique machines on Fisherman's Wharf — fortune tellers, orchestrions, and Laffing Sal cackling since the Playland days. Free to enter, quarters to play.
chill.bonus: Get your fortune from an antique machine and follow whatever it says for the rest of the day.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Exploratorium on Pier 15
chill.description: This legendary science museum has been rewiring adult brains since 1969 — give yourself two hours and you'll walk out with a completely different understanding of perception.
chill.bonus: Find the Tactile Dome and go through it — no phones, no map, in total darkness.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Wave Organ at Marina Green
chill.description: A sculpted acoustic instrument built into the breakwater at the tip of the Marina plays a living score of low gurgles and resonant tones using nothing but tidal action.
chill.bonus: Find the pipe with the deepest tone and sit with your ear to it for a full two minutes.

chill.title: Record Dig at Amoeba Music on Haight
chill.description: The West Coast's greatest independent record store commands a full city block and rewards anyone willing to lose two hours flipping through its genuinely staggering used vinyl selection.
chill.bonus: Buy one record you've never heard — based only on cover art — and play it that night.

chill.title: Afternoon at Alamo Square Park
chill.description: The Painted Ladies Victorian row and the downtown skyline stacked behind them from the park lawn is one of those rare city views that earns its postcard status in person.
chill.bonus: Find a spot on the grass, pick one stranger nearby, and guess their whole life story — then introduce yourself and see how wrong you were.

chill.title: Chinese American History at the Chinese Historical Society
chill.description: Tucked into a 1932 Julia Morgan building in Chinatown, this small museum holds a surprisingly moving account of how Chinese labor literally built California.
chill.bonus: Find one artifact or photo that genuinely stops you — read every word of its label before moving on.

chill.title: Read at City Lights Bookstore in North Beach
chill.description: Lawrence Ferlinghetti's legendary Beat-era bookstore on Columbus Avenue is still independently owned, still open late, and still lit like a place where ideas matter.
chill.bonus: Buy one book based solely on the first sentence — no reviews, no covers, no author recognition.

chill.title: Fog Watch from Hawk Hill in the Marin Headlands
chill.description: On summer mornings the fog pours through the Golden Gate like a slow-motion avalanche and Hawk Hill is the best seat in the house.
chill.bonus: Stay until the fog either fully clears or fully swallows the bridge — no leaving in the middle of the act.

chill.title: Wander the de Young Museum Sculpture Garden
chill.description: Even if you skip the galleries, the free outdoor sculpture garden at the de Young in Golden Gate Park is one of the city's most underused calm spots.
chill.bonus: Find one sculpture that makes you genuinely uncomfortable and sit with it for five full minutes.

chill.title: Afternoon at Sightglass Coffee SoMa
chill.description: A converted warehouse with serious coffee and even better people-watching anchors the slowly shifting SoMa neighborhood with genuine style.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone face-down for the entire visit — order by actually talking to the barista.

chill.title: Spend an Hour in the Japanese Tea Garden
chill.description: The oldest public Japanese garden in the US pulls you into a world of moon bridges, koi ponds, and raked gravel that makes the city noise genuinely disappear.
chill.bonus: Find the tallest pagoda, sit facing it, and stay completely still for 10 minutes without checking your phone.

chill.title: Sit in Dolores Park on a Sunny Saturday
chill.description: The Mission's hillside park is SF's living room — street food vendors, fog-free sunshine, city skyline, and every subculture in the city spread out on one slope.
chill.bonus: Strike up a conversation with the strangers nearest to you and find out one surprising thing about them.
